html_bullets.point: Tata Motors reported a 51% year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit to Rs 8,470 crore for Q4 FY25, with revenue from operations remaining flat at Rs 1.19 lakh crore. The Board recommended a final dividend of Rs 6 per share, subject to shareholder approval.

Net profit for Q4 FY25 declined 35% to ₹1,382 crore, compared to ₹2,126 crore in the same quarter last year, with total income remaining flat at ₹20,206 crore. The Board recommended a final dividend of ₹6 per share, pending shareholder approval.

Tata Motors reported mixed earnings for Q4 FY25, with profit exceeding estimates. Shareholders are voting on a proposed demerger to separate passenger vehicle and commercial vehicle operations, potentially unlocking value for investors.
Tata Motors achieved record revenues of ₹439.7K Cr and a net profit of ₹28.1K Cr for FY25, marking a strong performance despite external challenges. A final dividend of ₹6.00 per share was approved.
Tata Motors experienced a 9% rally amidst geopolitical tensions and a cyber threat alert issued by SEBI.

Tata Motors anticipates a strong rebound in electric vehicle sales in FY26, supported by new model launches such as Harrier.ev and Sierra.ev, after experiencing a 10% decline in FY25 sales due to reduced fleet sales linked to the withdrawal of the FAME II subsidy. Capex for FY26 is expected to remain similar to FY25's ₹8,400 crore.
Tata Motors led the electric vehicle market in India with 4,436 units sold in April 2025, contributing to a significant increase in electric passenger vehicle sales in the country.
Tata Motors plans to repurpose and responsibly recycle EV batteries, contributing to a more sustainable energy ecosystem.
Tata Motors experienced a single-digit decline in monthly EV sales in April, reflecting challenges faced by the passenger vehicle segment.

heading: Jaguar Land Rover and Free Trade Agreements

html_bullets.point: The India-UK free trade agreement is expected to enhance JLR's performance in India by allowing faster access to global cars at competitive prices. Reduction of US tariffs on UK auto exports was welcomed, but further details are needed to understand the full impact.

British Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced a historic trade deal with the US at Tata Motors' Jaguar Land Rover factory, reducing car export tariffs from 27.5% to 10% for a quota of 100,000 UK cars, benefiting the automotive industry significantly.

Tata Motors is expected to benefit from the duty-free import quota for electric vehicles under the new free trade agreement with the UK, lowering tariffs on automotive imports from over 100% to 10% under quotas.
Tata Motors Limited held a Court Convened General Meeting to discuss the Composite Scheme of Arrangement, which was approved by 99.9995% of Equity Shareholders.

The merger between Tata Motors Finance Limited and Tata Capital Limited was successfully sanctioned by the National Company Law Tribunal, aligning with Tata Motors' strategy to exit non-core businesses and focus on emerging technologies.
Tata Motors appointed M/s Parikh & Associates as Secretarial Auditors for a five-year term from April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2030, pending shareholder approval.
Re-appointment of Mr. K V Chowdary as Non-Executive Independent Director for a second consecutive term from October 27, 2025, to October 10, 2029, was announced, subject to shareholder approval.
